newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico toys petrochems sell-off solution - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico toys petrochems sell-off solution - paper.

text.p: Mexican government officials and congressmen are studying a solution for the petrochemicals privatization problem that arose out of the weekend's convention of the ruling party, Mexico City daily Reforma said Wednesday.

Citing congressmen from the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), Reforma said the escape plan is to sell off just 49 percent of shares of the 61 petrochemical plants and create a new state-owned company to hold a majority 51 percent.

Mexico's plans to privatize its secondary petrochemicals plants was virtually blocked over the weekend as PRI delegates voted to oppose the sell off, wanting the state to keep control of the oil, gas and oil derivatives industries. The PRI has legislative majorities.

The petrochemical sell-off has also faced stiff opposition, delaying the start of the privatizations, with numerous sectors seeing it as a threat to the sovereignty Mexico stands guard on state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) with articles within the Mexican constitution strictly governing Pemex's operation. Pemex currently runs the petrochemical plants.

National and international companies, including Terra and Farmland of the United States, have already placed bids for the first item on the block, a complex of ammonia plants in Cosoleacaque with annual sales of more than $400 million. The winner of that auction should have been named in April.
